subject: RFP: commercial approach and risk-sharing for inference consumption
summary: Commercial response to MakeTech RFP focused on committed token bands, burst/overage mechanics, smoothing/carry-forward protections, and a proposed risk-sharing SLA credit/rebate. Includes numeric examples and asks to schedule a follow-up to finalize legal redlines.
messages:
From: James Liu <james.liu@maketech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai; procurement@maketech.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP submission + clarifying questions on pricing approach

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is MakeTech's procurement package and the commercial worksheet portion we asked vendors to complete (MakeTech_RFP_Q3-2026.pdf). A few clarifying items we need answered in your commercial section:

- Do you offer volume-commit bands (monthly or annual) and what are typical per-token rates at each band?
- How do you bill for burst traffic above commit? Is there a hard cap on day-over-day spend increases we can apply?
- Do you offer smoothing/carry-forward protections for seasonality? If so, what is the lookback and carry-forward limit?
- We are evaluating a risk-sharing clause: if service fails to meet agreed latency/availability SLOs, is there a rebate mechanism that directly reduces the commercial invoice rather than a generic credit?
- What is your true-up cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual) and tolerances on overage reconciliation?

Please attach your commercial worksheet with an example math for a 500M committed token month and an 800M surge month. We'd appreciate a response by end of week.

Best regards,
James Liu
Senior Procurement Manager
MakeTech Systems
[attachment: MakeTech_RFP_Q3-2026.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: James Liu <james.liu@maketech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP submission + clarifying questions on pricing approach

Hi James —

Thanks for the RFP and the clear list of asks. I've attached our working commercial worksheet (redwood-pricing-model-v2.xlsx) with a worked example for the 500M commit vs 800M surge scenario you requested. High level summary below; the spreadsheet has line-by-line math you can drop into your TCO model.

Quick answers (more detail in attachment):
- Commit bands: monthly commits supported; we offer tiered per-token pricing at stepped thresholds.
- Overage: billed at a predefined overage multiplier with optional burst cushion and a 30-day carry-forward window option.
- Smoothing: we can provide a 20% monthly burst cushion by default and allow carry-forward of unused commit up to 30 days.
- Risk-sharing: we propose invoice-reducing performance credits tied to latency SLO misses (detailed formula enclosed).
- True-up cadence: monthly with an optional quarterly true-up for enterprise accounting preference.

Can we schedule a 45-minute call on Thursday 9/16 to walk the spreadsheet and align on the risk-sharing language? I'll include Marissa (pricing) and Karthik (legal lead) on the call.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-model-v2.xlsx

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[kimberly_park@redwood.ai]
[attachment: redwood-pricing-model-v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: James Liu <james.liu@maketech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@maketech.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP submission + clarifying questions on pricing approach

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple follow-ups after a first pass of the spreadsheet:

1) The overage multiplier you show is 1.25x baseline — can you provide a capped daily spend increase to limit procurement exposure for large surges? For example, no more than 50% day-over-day fiscal impact without prior notice.
2) For the risk-sharing rebate: can you show numeric examples? If we pay $X in an overage month and you miss the 99th percentile latency SLO twice, what is the net financial impact to MakeTech?
3) For smoothing/carry-forward: can we increase carry-forward to 45 days for Q4 seasonality?
4) Is there a biennial price-protection clause you support if we sign a multi-year commit?

If you can include examples for (1) and (2) in your next email that would be great.

Regards,
James

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: RFP submission + clarifying questions on pricing approach

Team — forwarding James' follow-ups. He needs firm answers/examples on capped daily spend, numeric risk-sharing rebate examples, and Q4 carry-forward flexibility. Draft below is what I'm planning to send back to MakeTech; please review numbers and legal/finance implications.

DRAFT commercial proposal (numbers for approvals):
- Commit: 500M tokens/month at $0.00075/token (monthly invoiced).
- Tiered bands (effective per-token price within month): 500M–1B: $0.00070; 1B–2B: $0.00062.
- Overage pricing: billed at 1.25x the effective per-token price for the band where overage occurs. Example: a single month with 800M tokens billed as 500M @ $0.00075 + 300M @ $0.00070, overage portion would be priced at 1.25x relevant rate.
- Burst/cap rule: daily spend increase cap of 50% vs preceding day's spend without prior notice; any excess flagged and billed subject to prior approval.
- Burst cushion & smoothing: standard 20% monthly cushion. For Q4 we can offer a one-time 45-day carry-forward on unused commit (limited to first contract year only).
- True-up: monthly; customer pays overage at month end with rolling 30-day reconciliation. Optional quarterly invoicing available for accounting.

Risk-sharing (performance credits):
- SLA: 99th-percentile generation latency SLO of 450ms regionally.
- Credit: for each distinct SLA breach window (>= 30 min contiguous breach impacting >5% of requests) Redwood will credit 5% of that month's invoice up to a cap of 10% of the monthly invoice.
- Overage rebate clause: if an overage month coincides with SLO breach, Redwood will rebate 25% of billed overage (i.e., 25% reduction on the overage line) in addition to the general SLA credit; rebate applied before any other usage credits.

Numeric example (requested):
- Baseline: 500M commit at $0.00075 = $375,000.
- Surge month: 800M total usage. Calculation: 500M @ $0.00075 = $375,000; 300M @ $0.00070 = $210,000 -> total billed usage = $585,000.
- Overage: 300M is within tiered band (no overage if within tier). If usage was 1,100M instead (600M over band): overage portion 100M would be billed at 1.25x applicable rate (assume applicable rate $0.00062 -> overage unit price = $0.000775 -> overage = $77,500).
- If a qualifying SLO breach occurs that month, Redwood would: (a) credit 5% of invoice up to 10% cap and (b) rebate 25% of the overage line. Using the 1,100M example: 5% invoice credit = 0.05 * (585,000 + 77,500) = $33,125 (applied to invoice), overage rebate = 0.25 * 77,500 = $19,375, net incremental cost to MakeTech for the overage reduces by the rebate amount.

Open items for legal/finance: are the credit caps and the overage rebate acceptable? Need to confirm whether we can expose rebate as an invoice reduction vs a credit memo (customer prefers invoice reduction).

Please weigh in on the numbers; if approved I'll send the formal commercial response back to James with clean examples and updated attachment.

Thanks,
Kim

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: RFP submission + clarifying questions on pricing approach

Kim / Karthik —

Looks good. A few suggested edits for better procurement reception:
- Make the daily spend cap language explicitly bill-impacting: "Redwood will not invoice daily system spend increases greater than 50% vs the prior day without documented notice; any excess will be held for review and subject to mutual written approval before billing."
- Increase the monthly performance credit cap to 10% (you already have 10% cap listed) but add a floor: if total invoice < $100,000, minimum credit considered $5,000 per qualifying breach to ensure materiality for small pilots.
- Offer a carry-forward increase to 45 days for Q4 (first-year only) as a written concession.
- For legal: we should keep the rebate as an invoice reduction if possible; if not, limit to credit memo for accounting reasons. Karthik, can you confirm tolerances?

I attached a cleaned commercial slide and SLA exception form for the legal team to sign off.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA-exception-form.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: James Liu <james.liu@maketech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@maketech.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFP submission + clarifying questions on pricing approach

Hi James —

Appreciate the follow-ups. Below is a concise commercial response and worked examples per your requests. The attached spreadsheet contains the full line-by-line math; I pulled the highlights here so your finance team can see the net effects quickly.

Proposed commercial terms (summary):
- Commit: 500M tokens/month (monthly billing) at $0.00075/token.
- Tiered effective prices within month: 500M–1B: $0.00070/token; 1B–2B: $0.00062/token.
- Overage: billed at 1.25x the applicable per-token price for the band where overage occurs.
- Burst daily spend cap: Redwood will not invoice daily spend increases >50% vs the prior day without documented notice; any flagged excess is subject to mutual review prior to billing.
- Smoothing/carry-forward: standard 20% monthly burst cushion; one-time Q4 first-year carry-forward increase to 45 days (to cover seasonality).
- True-up: monthly; optional quarterly invoicing upon request.

Risk-sharing & SLA credits (commercial mechanics):
- SLO: 99th-percentile generation latency <= 450ms (regional).
- Credit: for each qualifying SLA breach window (>= 30 minutes contiguous, impacting >5% of requests), Redwood will apply a 5% credit to that month's invoice; cumulative credits capped at 10% of the monthly invoice. For invoices < $100k, a minimum per-breach credit floor of $5,000 applies.
- Overage rebate: if an overage month coincides with a qualifying SLO breach, Redwood will rebate 25% of the billed overage amount. Rebates will be applied as an invoice reduction where permitted; otherwise as a credit memo.

Worked examples (attachment has line-by-line):
- 500M commit at $0.00075 = $375,000 monthly baseline.
- 800M usage month: 500M @ $0.00075 = $375,000; 300M @ $0.00070 = $210,000 -> usage billed = $585,000 (no overage if within tier).
- 1,100M usage month: billed usage = 500M @ $0.00075 ($375,000) + 500M @ $0.00070 ($350,000) + 100M overage @ 1.25x $0.00062 = $77,500 -> total billed = $802,500.
- If a qualifying SLO breach occurs that month: 5% invoice credit = $40,125 (applies up to 10% cap). Overage rebate = 25% * $77,500 = $19,375. Net incremental cost for the customer is reduced accordingly; full math is in the spreadsheet.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-model-v2.xlsx, SLA-exception-form.pdf.

Next steps: can we slot a 45-minute technical + commercial review on Mon 9/21 or Tue 9/22? If those don't work, suggest a time that does and we will accommodate. Once we align, we'll produce a short-term commercial exhibit for signature and a draft SOW.

Thanks and talk soon,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
[attachment: redwood-pricing-model-v2.xlsx, SLA-exception-form.pdf]
